Emily — great to connect last week. Following internal alignment, we want to make an ask that will materially speed SageBank's onramp and close schedule. Attaching a concise MVP requirements sheet (SageBank-MVP-requirements.xlsx).

High-level ask: can we surface a small set of enterprise guardrails and a scoped audit export capability ahead of our standard roadmap order so SageBank can complete their procurement sign-off next quarter? Specifically: 
- Tenant-level isolation routing (logical tenant pinning for enterprise customers)
- Per-request audit export (CSV export stub + S3 delivery hook)
- Additional telemetry headers for trace correlation (trace_id passthrough)

Why this matters: procurement & security have collectively said these three items are gating for formal legal + ops sign-off. If we can commit to a narrow delivery window, they are prepared to sign a 12-month reserved capacity deal (DEAL-9734-SAGE) and expedite procurement.

Requesting: 
1) Product/Eng feasibility check: can we carve a minimal, low-risk implementation for the three items above?
2) If feasible, a target timeline or a list of scoped compromises that would be acceptable to SageBank.

Monica / Priyom — looping you to help coordinate the MA P and to route to product. Karthik / Laura — please see the attachment; Ben is requesting an early feasibility/impact call this week if possible.

Thanks,
Ben

Monica / Ben — thanks for the context and the MVP sheet. Quick read and high-level feasibility notes below (short technical summary + recommended mitigation paths). Attachment: priority_impact_matrix.pdf (impact vs effort).

Summary: 
- Tenant-level isolation (routing/pinning): medium effort. We can deliver a safe, configuration-driven pinning in ~6–8 weeks if we scope it to logical routing (no kernel/runtime changes). A faster shim (4 weeks) could be done by routing at the proxy layer, but it lacks per-VM isolation guarantees.
- Per-request audit export: low effort if we implement a CSV export pipeline and S3 sink with a toggle. We can ship a first-cut in ~2–3 weeks (happy-path only; limited retention config).
- Trace_id passthrough: trivial (1 week) — minimal runtime changes required.

Tradeoffs and risks: 
- Fastest path requires us to accept a narrower SLA and limited retention for exports; procurement may require stronger guarantees.
- The full-scope tenant isolation (true compute affinity + enforced isolation) requires architectural work and potential infra commit — estimate 10–12 weeks.

Recommendations (2-path plan):
1) Fast-scope (ship quickly, low risk): implement proxy-layer pinning, CSV audit export to S3 with short-term retention, trace_id passthrough. ETA: 3–4 weeks.
2) Full-scope (long-term, hardened): implement routing + runtime affinity, encrypted export controls, retention policy, and audit trail. ETA: 10–12 weeks.

Request from Sales/CS: to prioritize fast-scope we need a formal business trigger — e.g., signed reserved capacity or an explicit product prioritization request tied to DEAL-9734-SAGE. Without that, we will queue behind other committed roadmap items.

Next step: recommend a 30-minute triage with engineering leads + security to confirm the fast-scope acceptance criteria. I'm free Fri 11:00–12:00 or Mon 09:00–10:00 PT.

Karthik
